question.text: What are the Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) measures under the IFSCA Guidelines when ML/TF risks are HIGH?

answer.text: Obtain additional customer information and update identification data more frequently; examine source of wealth and source of funds of the customer or Beneficial Owner; obtain Senior Management approval to commence or continue the relationship; conduct enhanced monitoring; and require the first payment through the customer's own bank account
Obtaining additional customer information and updating identification data more frequently
Examining source of wealth and source of funds of the customer or Beneficial Owner
Obtaining Senior Management approval to commence or continue the business relationship

explanation.text: The Logic: EDD measures under the IFSCA Guidelines include: (i) additional customer information and more frequent identification-data updates; (ii) examining source of wealth and funds of the customer or Beneficial Owner; (iii) recording the purpose behind transactions; (iv) Senior Management approval to commence or continue the business relationship; (v) enhanced monitoring with increased controls; and (vi) requiring the first payment to be routed through the customer's own bank account. The Trap: Each single-measure distractor is true on its own, which tempts a candidate to stop at one item. EDD is not 'more documents' — it includes deeper analysis of wealth sources, transaction purposes, Senior Management involvement, and the first-payment-from-own-account requirement, which is often overlooked. Note: The "first payment from the customer's own bank account" requirement is the EDD measure most often overlooked — it is just as mandatory as Senior Management approval and source-of-funds checks.
